# Group 5A Navigation Taxonomy — Expense Types, Forms and Fields, Accounting Administration, Map Invoice Concept Fields

Corpus searched: both `concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides` and `...-tools-guides` (2026_08).

---

## 1. Expense Types

**Click sequence** (`accessing-expense-types-acb02b63.md`):
> "1. Select Administration  Invoice. 2. From the Invoice Processing Admin menu, choose Expense Types."

Also stated in `expense-types-and-policies`/`expense-types-process-8b2dbb0e.md` as living in "Expense Types tool in Invoice Administration."

- **Aliases**: "Invoice Processing Admin > Expense Types" (primary); "Expense Types area of the Administrator" (`changing-the-status-of-an-expense-type-1e641b70.md`).
- **Tabs/steps on the page**: not tabs but a 3-step wizard when adding — Step 1: General (Name, Spend Category), Step 2: Policies, Step 3: Attendees (`adding-expense-types-97cac818.md`). Editing reopens the same steps (`edit-expense-types-c6d0b6fc.md`: "Click Next until you reach the Attendees tab").
- **Admin role**: "By default, only an administrator with Global rights can create or edit a new expense type. If the Group Create Rights policy setting is selected, then a group administrator can also create and edit expense types." (`adding-expense-types-97cac818.md`). Activation-per-policy is done separately in the **Policies** tool, not on this page.
- **Renamed/absorbed/split?** No — the page is present and current. It has a duplicate pair of near-identical topics for several actions (e.g., `editing-expense-types-87b972d0.md` vs `edit-expense-types-c6d0b6fc.md`; `change-the-status...-cf452b6a.md` vs `changing-the-status...-1e641b70.md`) — these read as legacy/rewrite duplicates covering the same UI, not a legacy/New-Experience split (no "New Experience" language found on any of them; treat as `uiVariant: undifferentiated`).
- **Coverage read**: Solid — access, add, edit, delete, and status-change are all separately documented with verbatim field tables (attendee checkbox table is thin-but-real).
- **Catalog tables**:
  - `list-of-spend-categories-8b2de886.md` — **"Available Spend Categories"** pipe table with columns Spend Category / Spend Category Code / Recommended Use / Description. Counted **~50 concrete entries** (verified via unique uppercase code strings, e.g. TRAIN, UTLTS). Not raw HTML (`grep -c "<table"` = 0). This is the catalog the extractors need for the Spend Category field on Step 1: General.
  - `spend-categories-3e18cb3b.md` is a short concept page, not the catalog itself — don't double-count it.

---

## 2. Forms and Fields (Invoice Processing Admin)

**Click sequence** (`accessing-the-forms-and-fields-page-8b2e27af.md`):
> "1. Click Administration  Invoice. 2. Under the Invoice Processing Admin menu, click Forms and Fields."

- **Aliases**: none beyond the standard "Administration > Invoice > Invoice Processing Admin > Forms and Fields."
- **Structure/tabs**: This page is driven by a **Form Type** selector (`select-a-form-type-36dec640.md`, `accessing-forms-e46897a3.md`), which then exposes two tabs:
  - **Fields** tab (`accessing-fields-17089536.md`, `working-with-the-forms-and-fields-page-8b2ea265.md`) — modify field attributes.
  - **Form Fields** tab (`accessing-forms-fields-d7c875b0.md`, `modifying-form-fields-f9433665.md`) — has a search box (label substring + magnifying glass) and per-form field trees.
- **Admin role**: "Invoice Configuration administrator" (unqualified/general) per `accessing-the-forms-and-fields-page-8b2e27af.md`. (Contrast with Capture Processing's separate page below, which requires the *Unrestricted* variant specifically.)
- **Renamed/absorbed/split?** **IMPORTANT FINDING — name collision, not a rename.** "Forms and Fields" is documented as **two structurally distinct pages** sharing one name:
  1. **Invoice Processing Admin > Forms and Fields** (this section) — the full field-modification tool with Form Type/Fields/Form Fields tabs, `Modify Field`/`Modify Fields` windows.
  2. **Capture Processing Admin > Forms and Fields tab** (see §2a below) — a tab inside a different admin tool (Capture Processing Admin), scoped only to OCR/verification form setup.
  Extractors must not conflate these — same label, different `page` nodes, different parent nav, different role gate.
- **Coverage read**: Good — access, modify-fields (single/attribute-level), and modify-form-fields (bulk/multi-select) are each documented, plus a large field-attribute reference table.
- **Catalog table**: `modifying-fields-b16a6078.md` contains the **Data Type → Control Type Options** mapping table (Amount/Boolean/Connected List/Date/Integer/List/Numeric/Text → their control types), plus the full Data Type enum (8 values: Amount, Boolean, Connected List, Date, Integer, List, Numeric, Text) and the Default Value Type enum (Copy Down / Copy Down from Purchase Order Header / None) and Access Rights enum (Modify / Read-only / Hidden). Small but fully enumerated and genuinely `validValues`-worthy. Markdown pipe table, not raw HTML.

### 2a. Forms and Fields tab (Capture Processing Admin) — related but separate page
Parent path: `accessing-capture-processing-admin-2fb515a6.md`:
> "The Invoice Configuration administrator (Unrestricted) role navigates to Administration > Invoice > Capture Processing Admin to open the page. The page opens to the Capture Processing view of the Forms and Fields tab."

- **Sibling tabs on Capture Processing Admin** (`using-the-capture-processing-admin-tool-8b2ae77c.md`): Forms and Fields, Task Definition, Email Administration, Supplier Email Administration, Other Settings.
- **Admin role**: "Invoice Configuration administrator (Unrestricted)" — explicitly the *Unrestricted* variant, distinct from the general role cited for the standalone Forms and Fields page.
- **Catalog table**: `configuring-forms-and-fields-in-capture-processing-7c14446c.md` has a **raw `<table>`** (`grep -c "<table"` = 1 → `fromRawHtmlTable: true` eligible) enumerating "Fields Supported for Capture for Client-Managed Capture Processing" — Header Fields (Vendor Name, Invoice Date, Invoice Number, Currency, Total Amount, Shipping, Tax, PO Number, Invoice Owner is configured, Vat 1, Vat Amount 1-4) and Line-Item Fields (Part Number, Description, Total (calculated), Quantity, Unit Price, PO Number, Vat 1, Vat Amount 2-4). Note the compressed ranges "Vat Amount 1-4" / "Vat Amount 2-4."
- **Tools-guides variant**: `forms-and-fields-dccd3d8c.md` (Tools Guides deliverable) is a thin end-user-facing restatement of the same Capture Processing Forms and Fields tab — confirms the tab exists but adds no new fields; use admin-guides as primary source.

---

## 3. Accounting Administration

**Click sequence** (`accessing-the-accounting-administration-page-64021b08.md`):
> "1. Select Administration  Invoice Admin. 2. Select Accounting Administration. The Account Codes tab of the Accounting Administration page appears."

- **Aliases**: "Invoice Admin" alias confirmed active here too.
- **Tabs**:
  1. **Account Codes** (default landing tab) — `account-codes-tab-2acab3a1.md`: left pane = account code hierarchy tree (root "Global," level 1 "Ledger," then configured levels); right pane = per-expense-type Account Code / Inherited Code / Inherited Level columns.
  2. **Accounting Structure** — reached via "Accounting Administration > Accounting Structure" (`accessing-the-ledger-a5dae897.md`, `accessing-the-account-code-hierarchy-page-edce1aa5.md`). Lists ledgers (Ledger Name/Ledger Code — `adding-a-new-ledger-1ef1c514.md`) and, per ledger, a "Modify Hierarchy" action opening the **Account Code Hierarchy for Ledger** page (adding/editing/deleting Segments: `adding-a-new-segment-d6dfb07b.md`, `editing-a-segment-f79aecf7.md`, `deleting-a-segment-62b49ad9.md`).
- **Admin role** (`required-roles-1f2a20f6.md`, verbatim): "The Shared Configuration administrator defines the ledger. The Invoice Configuration administrator: Defines the account code hierarchies / Maps the expense type/account codes. The Account Codes tool is available if the user has been assigned the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role." — three distinct role/task pairings, worth modeling separately.
- **Renamed/absorbed/split?** Not renamed. Note: "Ledgers" itself is documented as a **stub/pointer page** — `ledgers-1414170c.md`: "For information about ledgers, refer to the Concur Expense: Ledgers Setup Guide" — the Ledgers *concept* is authoritative in a different (Expense) guide even though the Accounting Structure tab is where ledgers are administered inside Invoice.
- **Coverage read**: Strong for Account Codes and Accounting Structure/segments; thin-by-design for the underlying Ledger concept (deliberately punted to Concur Expense docs — do not fabricate ledger fields from Invoice docs).
- **Catalog tables**:
  - `account-code-hierarchy-869f7eca.md` — enumerated criteria list: Invoice-related (Country, Currency, Policy, **"Org Unit 1-6"**, **"Custom 1-20"**), Invoice Line Item (Custom 1-20), Allocation-related (Custom 1-20). Compressed ranges present — "Org Unit 1-6" (expands to 6 concrete fields), "Custom 1-20" (expands to 20 concrete fields, appears 3 times in different scopes: Request, Line Item, Allocation — these are likely three *separate* field families despite the identical literal name, per-scope).
  - `adding-a-new-segment-d6dfb07b.md` — Segment Name options by Level: Request (Country, Currency, Custom 1-20, Org Unit 1-6, Policy Name), Line Item (Custom 1-20), Allocation (Custom 1-20). Same compressed-range caveat applies.
  - Both are small enumerated lists (not huge tables) but structurally important — every value is a genuine `validValues` candidate for the "Segment Name" list field.

---

## 4. Map Invoice Concept Fields

**Not found.** Exhaustive search (`grep -rli "map invoice concept\|concept field"` across both directories, plus "Map Invoice," "Concept," "mapping") returns **zero hits** for any page, alias, or breadcrumb matching this name. Related-but-distinct pages that do exist and might be confused with it:
- `field-mapping-e3881fa5.md` ("Field Mapping") — a **Peppol ↔ Concur Invoice field** reference table (not a "Concept Fields" admin page; it's a static integration-reference topic, not a configurable UI screen). Contains a large enumerated Peppol-field-to-Invoice-field table (~35+ rows) worth capturing separately if Peppol/e-invoicing is in scope for another group.
- `map-to-the-general-ledger-ada4de6b.md` ("Map to the General Ledger") — a short concept page about GL segment mapping philosophy, not a configuration screen with fields/tabs.

**Recommendation**: Report this target as absent from the 2026_08 corpus rather than force a match. If "Map Invoice Concept Fields" is a real screen name in some other SAP Concur product surface (e.g., unified Expense/Invoice data model "Concept" mapping used elsewhere in SAP DRC/Cloud Integration docs), it is not documented under CONCUR_INVOICE Professional Edition admin or tools guides as crawled.

---

fields.name: Connected List - Default Value Type

fields.sourceQuote:
Choose whether the copydown functionality automatically populates the field.
    
    -   Copy Down: Copy down allows an employee to enter information into a field that the system then automatically enters into duplicate fields on other pages. This option takes precedence over other methods of pre-populating fields such as the Exchange Rates feature.

For example, if you want to copy down the Country Code, the copydown source will be Employee.     Use caution when copying down connected list fields. The field values that are copied down are then subsequently validated upon save of the item. If the validation on one field fails, then that field and all fields at lower levels in that same connected list will be saved as blank. Copydown is executed upon creation of the item and may also be executed upon change of the copydown source. For example, a field that is copied from the report header to the expense entry would potentially be overwritten when the report header source field is edited.
    
    -   None: Indicates this field does not use copydown functionality.
        
    -   Constant: You can configure the first field in the connected list as a constant. This allows you to enter a default value that the system will then always enter for the employee when that selected field appears.

grounding: Verified 49 Forms-and-Fields candidates against the corpus. All represent real, documented controls — nothing here is fabricated or tenant-specific. Every failing quote's content is otherwise accurate and traceable to a real, contiguous span in the cited file — so all are 'repair' (fix the quote), never 'drop'. Two duplicate-labeled candidates (data-type/control-type table variants) fail for the same reason: the actual file is a markdown table whose cells are split across padded blank lines, not a flat single-line-per-row string, even though fromRawHtmlTable is correctly false (0 raw <table> tags). Recommended repair pattern throughout: prefer a single unbroken sentence within one list item/cell as the sourceQuote (these all verify cleanly) rather than joining across list items or table rows, since the corpus's list/table spacing is irregular and not safely reconstructable from memory. | refuter: Refuted 58 candidates for "Forms and Fields" against both guide directories (all source files verified; `grep -c "<table"` returns 0 on every one, so `fromRawHtmlTable: false` is correct throughout, and no New Experience variant of this page exists in the corpus, so `uiVariant: "undifferentiated"` is correct).

THE BIG FINDING — 18 DUPLICATE NODES. Eighteen entries are the same control, same file, same quote, twice. SECOND FINDING — 16 QUOTES ARE NOT VERBATIM. Every multi-line sourceQuote in the set fails locked rule 1. dependencies.condition: An expense type must first be created on the Expense Types page (New); only then can it be activated for a particular policy in the Policies tool, which is what makes it visible to employees.

dependencies.targetField: Active Expense Types for policy (status = Inactive)
dependencies.condition: Creating an expense type automatically produces its row in the Policies tool with status Inactive; the system will not use it in a policy until it is marked Active.
dependencies.sourceQuote: All new expense types appear in the Policies tool as Inactive. For the system to use an expense type in a policy, the expense type must be marked as Active.

dependencies.condition: Adding an expense type makes it appear in Account Codes so an account code can be associated with it; no further admin action is needed for the row to appear.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Makes it appear in Account Codes to associate the appropriate account code

dependencies.condition: After adding an expense type the administrator must go on to Account Codes and identify the natural account code for it, for General Ledger extraction.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Account Codes: Identify the natural account codes for expense types for the General Ledger (GL) extraction.

dependencies.sourceField: Expense type availability on an invoice
dependencies.condition: Within the selected policy an expense type is available for inclusion in an invoice only while its status is Active; Inactive makes it unavailable.
dependencies.sourceQuote: You have the option to set each expense type to Active or Inactive status within the selected policy. If a field is Active, it is available for inclusion in an invoice; however, if the field is Inactive, it is not available.

dependencies.condition: Step 2: Policies of the New/Modify Expense Type wizard can only be used to assign the expense type to a policy by an administrator holding Group Create rights.
dependencies.sourceQuote: You must have Group Create rights to assign the expense types to a policy.

dependencies.condition: By default only a Global-rights administrator can create or edit an expense type; a group administrator gains that ability only when the Group Create Rights policy setting is selected.
dependencies.sourceQuote: By default, only an administrator with Global rights can create or edit a new expense type. If the Group Create Rights policy setting is selected, then a group administrator can also create and edit expense types.

dependencies.targetField: Rights level of the administrator who created the expense type (Global vs. Group)

dependencies.sourceQuote: Group Invoice Configuration administrators cannot delete expense types created by Global Invoice Configuration administrators.

dependencies.condition: Deletion is blocked for the reserved Undefined, Shipping, and Tax expense types, because the system uses them for company card transactions and for standard shipping and tax information on an invoice.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Undefined, Shipping, and Tax expense types cannot be deleted. The system uses these expense types for either company card transactions or for standard shipping and tax information on an invoice.

dependencies.condition: Deleting an expense type immediately removes it from any active policy. (Already-submitted invoices keep the expense type attached.)
dependencies.sourceQuote: Deleting removes the expense type immediately from any active policy.

dependencies.sourceField: Invoice processing (an invoice can be processed)

steps.name: Stand up a new expense type end to end (create, activate per policy, assign account code)
steps.goal: Create a net-new invoice expense type and carry it all the way to employee visibility and correct GL posting. The corpus states this crosses three separate tools and will silently half-work if any leg is skipped: the expense type exists but nobody can pick it (no policy activation), or it is pickable but posts against an inherited/blank account code.

sequence.action: Navigate Administration > Invoice > Invoice Processing Admin > Expense Types, then select New to open Step 1: General of the New Expense Type page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and this is position 1 of the documented three-tool process: 'Identify expense type needs, including adding, editing, or deleting. | Expense Types tool in Invoice Administration' (expense-types-process-8b2dbb0e.md). Nothing downstream exists until the record does — the same guide says adding it 'Makes it appear in the Policies  Active Expense Types for policy page with a status of Inactive' and 'Makes it appear in Account Codes to associate the appropriate account code' (adding-expense-types-97cac818.md). ROLE GATE, also corpus-stated: 'By default, only an administrator with Global rights can create or edit a new expense type. If the Group Create Rights policy setting is selected, then a group administrator can also create and edit expense types.'

sequence.action: On Step 1: General, type the expense type name into the Name field
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED that Name must precede Spend Category, and this is the non-obvious one: 'The Spend Category list will show the top three recommended spend categories based on what expense type the admin has entered in the Name field. The remaining spend categories are listed in alphabetical order' (adding-expense-types-97cac818.md). Pick the category first and the recommendation ranking is computed against an empty Name — the full 50-value list is still offered, so nothing errors, you just lose the assist.

sequence.action: On Step 1: General, choose a value from the Spend Category list
sequence.rationale: Belongs on Step 1 with Name because the wizard will not return here without re-entering Modify. The corpus enumerates 50 concrete categories (list-of-spend-categories-8b2de886.md) and describes the field only as classification — 'allows you to define the overall category of spend with which the expense type is associated. In a future release, this information will be used in the SAP Concur reporting solution.' No documented downstream control keys off this value, so it does not gate later steps; it is sequenced here purely because Step 1 is where it lives.

sequence.action: Choose Next to advance from Step 1: General to Step 2: Policies
sequence.rationale: The corpus documents Add as a strict 3-step wizard — 'Choose Next.' then 'In Step 2: Policies...' then 'Click Next.' then 'Step 3 Attendees appears.' (adding-expense-types-97cac818.md). The steps are gated in order; there is no documented way to jump to Attendees without passing through Policies.

sequence.action: On Step 2: Policies, select the policies to which this expense type will be assigned
sequence.rationale: Assignment must happen inside the wizard because Step 3: Attendees renders per policy — 'For each policy selected in the Policies step, it will show a set of check boxes for selecting the appropriate attendee-related functions.' Select no policies here and Step 3 has nothing to configure against. SECOND ROLE GATE, corpus-stated and distinct from the create right: 'You must have Group Create rights to assign the expense types to a policy.'

sequence.action: Choose Next to reach Step 3: Attendees, then select Done to commit the expense type
sequence.rationale: Done is the commit point for the whole wizard ('7. Select Done.'). Attendee check boxes on Step 3 are optional here — the corpus says they 'are necessary only for expense types that use the attendee fields' — and a separate documented edit path exists ('Click Next until you reach the Attendees tab', edit-expense-types-c6d0b6fc.md), so a non-attendee expense type can pass straight through.

sequence.action: Open the Policies tool, select the policy, choose Expense Types, select the new expense type and choose Activate
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED position 2 of the three-tool process and the single most-missed leg: 'Once you have created a new expense type, you must activate that expense type for a particular policy for it to appear to the employee in Concur Invoice. You do this within the Policies tool.' (adding-expense-types-97cac818.md). Reinforced by expense-types-and-policies-a01e2537.md: 'All new expense types appear in the Policies tool as Inactive.' Skip this and step 1-6 produce an expense type that is invisible to every employee. FIELD LEFT BLANK DELIBERATELY: the Policies page is already in the graph but its Activate/Deactivate control was not verified in the Group 5A field pass, so naming one here would invent a field. Note the near-duplicate control expenseTypeActiveStatusAction ('Active' / 'Activate' / 'Deactivate') and the read-only expenseTypeStatusDisplay ('Active' / 'Inactive') were captured under Expense Types — the corpus documents the status change under the Policies selection flow (changing-the-status-of-an-expense-type-1e641b70.md) while pointing back at Expense Types for authoring ('You create and manage the expense types listed on this page from the Expense Types area of the Administrator'), so which page node truly owns the button is UNRESOLVED in the corpus.

sequence.action: Open Administration > Invoice Admin > Accounting Administration, select the target node in the Account Codes hierarchy left pane, and type the code into the Account Code column for the new expense type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED position 3 of the three-tool process: 'Assign the appropriate account code. | Account Codes tab in the Accounting Administration tool in Invoice Administration.' It sits last because the expense type must already exist to appear as a row — the Expense Type column 'shows all expense types in the Invoice system (regardless of the associated policy and regardless of whether the expense type is currently in use)' (account-codes-tab-2acab3a1.md). Documented constraints: 'up to 20 alphanumeric characters (not case sensitive)', 'There is no validation on these fields. Two or more expense types can have the same account code.' THIRD ROLE GATE: 'The Account Codes tool is available if the user has been assigned the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role.' (required-roles-1f2a20f6.md).

sequence.action: Read the Inherited Code and Inherited Level columns for the new expense type before saving, then select Save
sequence.rationale: INFERRED ORDERING (the corpus documents the columns and the Save action but never states 'check inheritance before you save'). Grounding for why it belongs here: 'This column displays the account code from a previous level. If nothing is entered in the Account Code field for this level, this is the code that will be used' and Inherited Level 'displays the level at which the account code in the Inherited Code column is defined' (account-codes-tab-2acab3a1.md). A blank Account Code is therefore not an error state — it silently posts the parent level's code, so reading inheritance is the only documented way to tell a deliberate inherit from a forgotten entry. Save is corpus-stated last: '3. Select Save.' (adding-and-editing-account-codes-4b9ffdde.md).

steps.name: Bulk-load or rename expense types with account codes via Expense Type Import
steps.goal: Create, rename, activate and account-code many expense types in one pass instead of walking the 3-step wizard per type. The import collapses the three-tool process into one spreadsheet, which is exactly why the prerequisites have to be true BEFORE upload — the file references ledgers and policies by name and cannot create them.

sequence.action: On the Accounting Structure tab, confirm (or add) the ledger whose name you will type into the spreadsheet's Ledger column
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED dependency, read off the import column definition rather than a procedure: the Ledger column is 'Ledger name for the associated Account Code hierarchy. NOTE: If you leave this field blank, it will be assigned to the Global ledger.' (available-field-formats-8b49a3d9.md). The spreadsheet resolves a ledger by NAME — it does not create one — so a typo or a not-yet-created ledger does not fail loudly, it silently lands the account code on the Global ledger. Ledger Name is capped at 'no more than 40 characters in length' and, for Peppol sites, 'Customers using Peppol Integration must always set the Ledger Name as "Default"' (adding-a-new-ledger-1ef1c514.md).

sequence.action: Confirm the exact policy names you will list in the spreadsheet's Policy column (or decide to use the literal value All)
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED that the column is name-matched against existing policies: 'Policy | Comma separated list | List of all policies to apply the import to. Use the value All to update all policies.' (available-field-formats-8b49a3d9.md). Same failure shape as the ledger — the import consumes policy names, it does not author policies, so this has to be settled before the file is built. FIELD LEFT BLANK: Policies is in the graph but no verified Group 5A field names its policy-name control.

sequence.action: Go to Administration > Invoice > Expense Type Import (left menu) and download the expense type spreadsheet template from the link on the page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED entry point and first documented step of the import: access is 'Choose Administration   Invoice.' then 'Select Expense Type Import (left menu)' (access-the-invoice-processing-expense-type-import-page-3f5d3994.md), and step 1 is 'On the Expense Type Import page, select link.' then 'Select a location on your computer to save the spreadsheet.' (step-1-download-the-expense-type-spreadsheet-bbd21911.md). Download precedes populate because the corpus warns 'The user should not delete the values in the spreadsheet header row' — the header row is the contract. NAV NOTE: Expense Type Import is documented as a left-menu sibling under Administration > Invoice, NOT under the Invoice Processing Admin submenu that carries the Expense Types page itself; the import fields are nonetheless carried on the Expense Types page node in this graph.

sequence.action: In the downloaded template, set every cell's number format to Text, then populate the Expense Type Name column
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and it is a hard fail, not a warning: 'The user must ensure that all cells in the spreadsheet have a number format of text before the user uploads them... If the client does not format the cells as text, the import will fail.' The same topic flags the specific trap that re-breaks it after you have already formatted: 'If you use the Replace feature in Excel... cells formatted as text become general format after using Replace.' (step-2-populate-template-with-expense-type-data-43344980.md). Expense Type Name is the key column — 'New or existing expense type name in the default language. This field is required for client specified expense types.'

sequence.action: Populate New Expense Type Name ONLY on rows that are renames, leaving it as the corpus specifies for create rows
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED semantics: 'Changes an existing expense type name to the name specified in this field' (available-field-formats-8b49a3d9.md), and 'Use the New Expense Type Name field in the Excel spreadsheet provided through the user interface to update an existing name to a new Expense Type name' (step-2-populate-template-with-expense-type-data-43344980.md). It is sequenced immediately after Expense Type Name because the pair is read together — the old name identifies the row, the new name replaces it. CONTRADICTION TO CARRY: the same table's preamble asserts 'All fields are required', which cannot be literally true of a rename-only column on a create row; the corpus never reconciles this, so do not infer a blank-is-allowed rule from the field description alone.

sequence.action: Populate Spend Category with a spend category name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED that this column is name-matched against the published catalog, not free text: 'This field defines the overall category of spend with which the expense type is associated. Enter the spend category name in this field. More Information: For more information, refer to the List of Spend Categories and Codes section in this guide.' (available-field-formats-8b49a3d9.md). Format is 'Use default language'. The 50-value catalog verified for the UI spendCategory field is the same source list, so the import has no recommendation assist — there is no Name-driven top-three reordering in the spreadsheet path.

sequence.action: Populate Ledger with the ledger name confirmed in order 1, then Account Code with the code for the desired hierarchy node
sequence.rationale: These two columns are the reason order 1 exists, and they must be filled as a pair: Ledger is the 'Ledger name for the associated Account Code hierarchy' and Account Code is the 'Account code for the desired hierarchy node' (available-field-formats-8b49a3d9.md). CORPUS-STATED fallback, and it is the silent one: 'NOTE: If you leave this field blank, it will be assigned to the Global ledger.' A blank Ledger column does not reject the row — it re-homes the account code.

sequence.action: Populate Account Code for the hierarchy node named by the Ledger column
sequence.rationale: Sequenced after Ledger because the code is meaningless without the hierarchy that scopes it — the column is defined as the code 'for the desired hierarchy node', and the interactive equivalent (account-codes-tab-2acab3a1.md) resolves codes by position in the ledger's hierarchy tree. INFERRED: the corpus does not state that the import validates the code, but the UI-side rule 'There is no validation on these fields' means a wrong code will import cleanly and post wrong.

sequence.action: Populate Policy (comma-separated names, or All) and Activate? (Y or N), then on the Expense Type Import page select Choose File, select the spreadsheet, select Open, and select Upload Your Data
sequence.rationale: Activate? is the import's substitute for the manual Policies-tool activation from ConfigStep 01 — 'Y/N | Define whether or not the expense type is active in the selected policies' — so it is only meaningful once Policy names it a scope, which is why the pair sits together and last. Upload is CORPUS-STATED verbatim as the final step: 'On the Invoice Processing Expense Type Import page, select Choose File... Navigate to the correct location and select the expense type spreadsheet to upload... Select Open... On the Expense Type Import page, select Upload Your Data.' (step-3-upload-the-expense-type-spreadsheet-bd22dc81.md).

steps.name: Add a custom field to an invoice form and set its behaviour
steps.goal: Take a Custom or Org Unit field from raw data type through to a governed, correctly-typed, correctly-permissioned control sitting in the right place on a live invoice form. This is the sequence with the most one-way doors in Group 5A — the data type becomes unchangeable the moment anyone uses it.

sequence.action: Navigate Administration > Invoice > Invoice Processing Admin > Forms and Fields, then choose the target form type from the Form Type list
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED as the literal first move on this page: 'The first step in using Invoice Forms and Fields is selecting a form type. This list displays the various form types available for configuration. Selecting one of these form types causes the system to update the tabs with the forms and form fields for this form type.' (select-a-form-type-36dec640.md). Every later tab is scoped by this selection — the Fields tab procedure re-states it as its own step 1 ('On the Forms and Fields page, in the Form Type list, select the desired form type. Select the Fields tab.', accessing-fields-17089536.md). It also gates control-type availability downstream (see order 4). NOTE: the Form Type dropdown's options are never enumerated verbatim anywhere in the corpus — the eight captured values are the closest documented list, not a screen reading.

sequence.action: On the Fields tab, select the field and choose Modify Field (or double-click the field name) to open the Modify Fields window, and confirm the Field Name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED procedure: 'On the Fields tab, click the desired field to modify. Click Modify Field or double-click the field name. The Modify Fields window appears.' (modifying-fields-b16a6078.md). Field-level attributes are set here, BEFORE the field is placed on any form, because this is the site-wide definition: 'Underlying name of the field (64 characters). This is the name used to reference this field, regardless of which form is used. The field name is also the default form-field label.' This matches the documented process order: step 1 is 'On the Forms and Fields page: Set the field default settings' and only step 3 is 'Add all required fields to your required forms' (forms-fields-lists-and-validations-configuration-process-76d94b3b.md, which prefaces the list with 'typically in the order shown').

sequence.action: In the Modify Fields window, set Data Type
sequence.rationale: THE ONE-WAY DOOR, corpus-stated twice over: 'The data type is configurable _only_ for Custom and Org Unit fields. All other fields have fixed data types associated to the database column that holds the field value. Once anyone has used the data type in an invoice, you will be unable to change it on this page.' (modifying-fields-b16a6078.md). Get this wrong and the only remedy is a different field. It also must precede Control Type because the window is reactive: 'Note that when you select from the Data Type list, the window refreshes and provides other applicable fields.' Eight enumerated values: Amount (currency), Boolean, Connected List, Date, Integer, List, Numeric (floating point), Text.

sequence.action: In the same window, set Control Type from the options the chosen Data Type exposes
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED conditional: 'Allows you to select the control type users employ for data entry in the form. The option selected in the Data Type field determines the options that appear here.' The mapping table is explicit — Amount->Edit; Boolean->Check Box, Boolean List; Connected List->Edit (w/ Connected List Helper); Date->Edit (w/ Date Helper); Integer->Edit; List->Drop-down List, Edit (w/ List Helper); Numeric->Edit; Text->Edit, Multi-line Edit, Launch URL (Single-line), Launch URL (multi-line). THREE-WAY GATE worth encoding: 'The Launch URL control type will only appear if the following conditions are true: The Form Type is Line Item Details / The Data Type is Text / There is at least one application connector configured and enabled' — so if Launch URL is the goal, order 1's Form Type choice was already load-bearing and an application connector must exist outside this page. CONTRADICTION TO CARRY: the guide's separate Terminology control-types table gives a DIFFERENT set (it lists Integer and Amount as control types and omits Connected List); the corpus never reconciles the two, and both were captured.

sequence.action: Set the data-type-conditional attributes that the refreshed window now exposes — e.g. Default Max Length for Text, or the connected list definition name for Connected List
sequence.rationale: Position is forced by the window's own reactivity, corpus-stated: 'When you select Text, you may provide the maximum length of the field. When you select Connected List, you may provide the name of the connected list definition.' Default Max Length carries its own hedge — 'This field may or may not appear depending on the option selected in the Data Type field' — so a crawler must treat its absence as a valid state, not a miss.

sequence.action: If Data Type is List or Connected List, create the backing list before returning to finish the field
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED as a distinct page in the documented ordering: step 4 of the configuration process is 'On the List Management page: Identify and create the lists needed for the invoice forms', sitting between 'Add all required fields to your required forms' and 'Add or modify any of the field properties to fit the forms' (forms-fields-lists-and-validations-configuration-process-76d94b3b.md). ORDERING CAVEAT — the corpus places List Management AFTER form placement, whereas this sequence places it before, because the Connected List data type asks for 'the name of the connected list definition' inside the Modify Fields window. That reordering is INFERRED from the field description, not corpus-stated; the documented order is the one quoted above. FIELD LEFT BLANK: List Management is a valid edge target but has no verified Group 5A fields.

sequence.action: Set Default Value Type, and if Copy Down is chosen, set Copy Down Source, the source Field, and Copy Down Only If Empty
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED conditional chain — Copy Down Source is '(Only appears if _Copy Down_ is selected in the Default Value Type list)', and so is Copy Down Only If Empty. Enumerated: Default Value Type = Copy Down / Copy Down from Purchase Order Header / None; Copy Down Source = Employee / Purchase Order Header / Payment Vendor / Purchase Request Details. Sequenced after data type because copydown pairs a source field to this field and the types must line up. The corpus is explicit about precedence, which matters if a value later appears to be ignored: 'This option takes precedence over other methods of pre-populating fields such as the Exchange Rates feature.' Copy Down Only If Empty is the overwrite guard: 'Select this option if, on copydown action, only those fields with no data should be populated. Otherwise, the copydown will overwrite all data.'

sequence.action: Set Site Required and Access Rights, then Save the Modify Fields window
sequence.rationale: These two interact and the corpus states the trap outright: Access Rights is Modify / Read-only / Hidden, and 'If a field is required, you should not mark it Hidden.' Site Required is the broader blast radius — 'Determines whether the field is required in the form. If there is a check in this box, this field appears on all forms of the corresponding type' — so setting it changes every form under the Form Type picked in order 1, not just the one you are working on. Save closes the field-level definition: '4. Make any necessary changes. 5. Click Save.' (modifying-fields-b16a6078.md).

sequence.action: On the Forms tab, select the target form(s), choose Add Fields, select the field in the Add Fields to Forms window, and choose Add Fields to confirm
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED step 3 of the documented process — 'Add all required fields to your required forms' — and the verbatim procedure: 'On the Forms tab, select the desired forms. To select multiple forms, use Shift+click or Ctrl+click. Click Add Fields. The Add Fields to Forms window appears. Select the fields to add to the form. Use Shift+click or Ctrl+click for multiple fields. Click Add Fields.' (adding-fields-to-a-form-069da023.md). It sits AFTER the field-level definition because a field defined wrong and then placed must be fixed once centrally, not per form — the Field Name is 'used to reference this field, regardless of which form is used.'

sequence.action: On the Form Fields tab, expand the form with the plus sign and drag-and-drop the new field into position
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and only possible once the field is on the form: 'On the Form Fields tab, click the plus sign () next to the desired form name. Rearrange a field by dragging and dropping it to a new location of the form.' (rearranging-form-fields-846e3ab4.md). Per-form overrides also live on this tab — 'To modify a single form field, double-click the form field name. The Modify Form Fields window appears' — and the corpus notes the window contents shift the same way the field-level one does: 'Just like the Modify Fields window, the fields that appear in the Modify Form Fields window differ depending on the selections made for the data type, control type, and so on.' (modifying-form-fields-f9433665.md).

sequence.action: Set Default Validation on the field last
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED as the final step of the documented process, and the corpus explains why it is last: 'Add or create validations. To perform this task successfully, the administrator must first identify the fields that need validation.' (forms-fields-lists-and-validations-configuration-process-76d94b3b.md) — you cannot identify what needs validating until the form is assembled. The field itself is conditional: 'Allows you to select a validation routine to run against the field. Note: This field may or may not appear, depending on the option selected in the Data Type field.' The corpus deliberately punts the routine definitions elsewhere ('refer to the Shared: Validations Setup Guide'), so do not expect the validation catalog in this corpus.

steps.name: Define an account-code hierarchy segment for a ledger and expose its driving field on the invoice form
steps.goal: Make account codes resolve on something richer than ledger+expense type — e.g. by division or cost centre — without producing the documented silent failure where the hierarchy looks correct in Accounting Administration but resolves to null at invoice save because the driving field was never put on the form.

sequence.action: Navigate Administration > Invoice Admin > Accounting Administration, open the Accounting Structure tab, select New, and enter Ledger Name and Ledger Code
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED as step 1 of the documented three-step accounting build ('Step 1: Defining the Company's Ledger(s)', 'Step 2: Defining the Expense Account Code Hierarchy', 'Step 3: Account Codes Procedures'), and the dependency is stated inside the ledger topic itself: 'Once you have added a new ledger, the Shared Config administrator can add the accounting structure components.' (adding-a-new-ledger-1ef1c514.md). Hierarchy hangs off a ledger — the Account Codes tree's 'root node is Global. Level one is for Ledger' (account-codes-tab-2acab3a1.md). ROLE SPLIT, corpus-stated: 'The Shared Configuration administrator defines the ledger' while 'The Invoice Configuration administrator: Defines the account code hierarchies / Maps the expense type/account codes' (required-roles-1f2a20f6.md) — these are two different people, which is the real reason this is a separate step and not one continuous sitting. NOTE: the corpus deliberately punts the ledger concept out of Invoice — 'For information about ledgers, refer to the Concur Expense: Ledgers Setup Guide' (ledgers-1414170c.md) — so ledger_name and ledger_code are the only ledger fields documented here.

sequence.action: Enter Ledger Code alongside the name before leaving the new ledger row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED that this value is consumed by a downstream tool and is effectively unforgiving: 'The Ledger Code value must be unique and should be logical. The system uses this code as a criterion in the Import/Extract Administrator tool. If you define a code that is not readily recognizable, it may not be located by the system.' (adding-a-new-ledger-1ef1c514.md). It sits with the name because both are entered on the single new line the New button creates ('A new line appears in the list. Enter the required information.').

sequence.action: On the Accounting Structure tab select the ledger under Ledger Name, then select Modify Hierarchy to open the Account Code Hierarchy for Ledger page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED navigation, and the corpus warns what you will see: 'Select the ledger you want to affect under Ledger Name. Select Modify Hierarchy to display the Account Code Hierarchy for Ledger page.' followed by 'Note: This page is blank if you have not yet added segments to the ledger. There are no default values.' (accessing-the-account-code-hierarchy-page-edce1aa5.md). A blank page here is the expected state for a new ledger, not a load failure — do not treat it as an error and do not expect seeded segments.

sequence.action: Select New to add a segment row, then set Level (Request, Line Item, or Allocation) FIRST
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED that Level drives the Name options and therefore must be set first: 'Select Request, Line Item, or Allocation. The Name options will change, depending on which level you select.' (adding-a-new-segment-d6dfb07b.md). Level also determines WHERE the value is read from at invoice save, which is the substantive choice: 'If you select Request, the system uses the data held in the field for the invoice when looking up the account code for the expense type... it is possible for an employee to have one division on the invoice header, which is copied down from the employee profile, and another division assigned on the Distributions page for one or more line item entries. Depending on the level at which the expense account code hierarchy is defined, a different account code could be assigned to the entry.' (account-code-hierarchy-869f7eca.md).

sequence.action: Set Segment Name from the options the chosen Level exposes, optionally reorder the segments, then select Save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED conditional enumeration: Request offers Country, Currency, Custom 1-20, Org Unit 1-6, Policy Name; Line Item offers Custom 1-20; Allocation offers Custom 1-20 (adding-a-new-segment-d6dfb07b.md). COMPRESSED RANGES — 'Custom 1-20' is one literal option string denoting twenty concrete fields and 'Org Unit 1-6' denotes six; the same literal 'Custom 1-20' appears at all three levels and, per the hierarchy concept topic, these are scope-distinct families (invoice, invoice line item, allocation), not one shared set. Segment ORDER is itself configuration, corpus-stated: 'The fields used to define these segments are listed in the order to be used within the hierarchy to define the necessary accounts' (step-2-defining-the-expense-account-code-hierarchy-4a179387.md) and the procedure offers '(Optional) If you wish to, reorder the segments as necessary' before 'Select Save. The new segment is added to the ledger and the Accounting Administration page appears.' MINIMUM, corpus-stated: 'Each ledger must have at least one expense type account code segment.' CONTRADICTION TO CARRY: the concept topic lists the invoice-related criteria as Country, Currency, Policy, Org Unit 1-6, Custom 1-20 — 'Policy', not 'Policy Name' as the segment procedure has it; both were captured, neither is corrected by the other.

sequence.action: For each field named as a segment, select the matching Form Type and add that field to every invoice form used by employees on this ledger
sequence.rationale: THE SILENT-FAILURE STEP, and it is CORPUS-STATED at length: 'In addition, the selected fields must be added to the invoice forms that are used by the employees that use this ledger. If the fields are not located on the invoice form, it is possible that the account codes will not resolve properly, and that the employee receives an error. For example, assume that the Org Unit 2 field is set up as Division in the expense account code hierarchy and is selected for the invoice.
